messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: QTL-specific covariate interactions
parts:
Hi All,
I have some QTL models, where I want to test the significance of a second QTL (and QTL*covariate interaction) in the context of a less complex model.

1: Y ~ Q1 + Q2 + covar
2: Y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q2*covar + covar
3: Y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q1*covar + covar
4: Y ~ Q1 + Q1*covar + Q2*covar + covar

So, to get P-values for the Q2 term, I plan to calculate permutations for the 1st and 4th model with the following covariates:
1: scanone(..., addcovar= data.frame(genotypes@Q1, covar), intcovar=NULL)
4: scanone(..., addcovar= data.frame(genotypes@Q1, covar), intcovar=data.frame(covar))

However, it is not clear to me how (or if it is possible) to get permutation tests for the Q2 term in the 2nd and 3rd models.

Any advice is appreciated,
John

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL-specific covariate interactions
parts:
My approach is to do permutations just with the covariate (no QTL genotypes in the addcovar data frame).

Let's add model 0: Y ~ Q1 + cover

In comparing 1 to 0, I'd look at

operm_10 <- scanone(..., addcovar=covar, intcovar=NULL, n.perm=1000)

In comparing 2 to 0, I'd look at

operm_20 <- scanone(..., addcovar=covar, intcovar=covar, n.perm=1000)

In comparing 3 to 1 (is there a Q1 x covar interaction, I'd look at paired permutations with and without the interaction term:

set.seed(20150807)
operm_10 <- scanone(..., addcovar=covar, intcovar=NULL, n.perm=1000)
set.seed(20150807)
operm_30 <- scanone(..., addcovar=covar, intcovar=covar, n.perm=1000)
operm_31 <- operm_30 - operm_10

I'm not sure I understand what's going on with model 4, or what you want to compare it to.

When you talk about tests of significance, it should be for a comparison between two models.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL-specific covariate interactions
parts:
Including the genotypes doesn't quite work, as they end up being made independent of the rest of the genome. My approach has been to use the null hypothesis of no QTL as an approximation of the distribution in the presence of a QTL. With linked QTL, this won't work.

Two alternatives:

- a parametric bootstrap (simulate data under the fitted single-QTL model)
- a stratified permutation test (permute the phenotypes within each stratum defined by the genotype at the first QTL)

karl
